title: Memory-lane quant sensitivity sweep — AWQ & GPTQ layout experiments (Aug 2027)
body:
Purpose

Quick exploratory sweep to test whether model weight layout (contiguous per-row vs. interleaved vector-lane packing) materially changes the AWQ and GPTQ runtime trade-offs we see in our multi-arch kernels. Motivation came from odd memory-bound 95th p99 tails on 1-shot workloads in eu-west-1 yesterday (see Slack thread #perf-urgent). Hypothesis: AWQ-friendly layouts reduce cache-line fetches and improve steady-state throughput for medium sequence lengths (128-512) on Hopper and Blackwell, while some GPTQ kernels prefer contiguous row-major layouts for fused GEMM paths.

Scope and decisions

- Focus on two quant pipelines: AWQ 2-stage (blockwise + per-row scale) and GPTQ (post-training static granularity).
- Test two memory layouts: contiguous-per-row (default), and interleaved 32-lane packing (vector-lane-first).
- Evaluate on three kernels: fused-matmul (our primary CUDA + Triton path), vectorized-ntt (experimental microkernel), and fallback cuBLAS path for baseline.
- Models: open-13B (base), open-70B-lite (reduced attention variants) to check scaling. Use trimmed prompt corpus of 120 conversational prompts and 50 synthetic long-context prompts.
- Hardware: A100-80GB (legacy), H100-80GB, and Blackwell-BW1 (software-based kernel compiled for BW ISA).

Perf metrics captured

- throughput_tokens_per_sec (average over 1000 inferences)
- p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, p99_latency_ms
- GPU SM occupancy and achieved memory bandwidth (profiling counters)
- end-to-end cost-estimate (tokens / GPU-second)
- quality delta: relative logprob on held-out validation set and small LM-eval subset (LAMBADA + PIQA) expressed as percentage change vs float32 baseline

Methodology / harness notes

- Used local bench harness (scripts/bench/quant_layout_sweep) which instantiates identical input streams to avoid variance. Each config ran 1200 samples; first 200 warmup excluded.
- Kernel variants compiled via nightly builder (commit sha referenced in linked_artifacts).
- For AWQ flows we disabled our automatic prefix cache to avoid masking memory effects.
- For each (model, kernel, layout, hw) triple we measured counters with Nsight compute and captured perf trace (lightweight sampling every 50ms).
- All runs repeated 3x; reported numbers are median.

Key observations (short summary)

1) H100: interleaved (lane-packed) layout improved throughput by 12-18% for AWQ on fused-matmul kernel at seq_len 128-256. p95 improved ~10%. GPU memory bandwidth utilization increased by ~8 percentage points, and L2 hit ratio improved slightly.

2) A100: wins were smaller (3-7%) and inconsistent across sequence lengths. For long contexts (512+) contiguous-per-row regained parity or slightly outperformed lane-packed layout on GPTQ fused-matmul.

3) Blackwell: lane-packed layout gave biggest tail improvements on vectorized-ntt (p99 down by 22%) but increased kernel launch overheads, so short prompt latency p50 worsened by ~5% unless batching >= 4.

4) GPTQ path: generally preferred contiguous row-major layout on fused-matmul when using our autotuned kernel variants — likely due to prefetch strides in the GEMM microcode. AWQ path benefits more from lane-packing due to smaller per-block quant tables and more contiguous access to scale factors.

5) Quality: relative logprob change vs fp32 was <0.8% for all configs (within noise) except one AWQ+lane-packed+70B run where we saw 1.6% degradation on a small subset of prompts with long numerical sequences. Needs follow-up but not catastrophic.

Profiling deep-dive notes

- Nsight traces show that lane-packed AWQ reduces uncoalesced global loads inside the quant-decode loop by ~30% on H100. This matches the higher sustained memory throughput.
- For GPTQ fused path, contiguous layout enables larger continuous GEMM tiles; in our autotuner the tiling heuristic picks larger k-tiles giving better compute utilization.

Open hypotheses / experiments to prioritize

- H1: Dynamic layout selection at model load can be beneficial. Decision logic: if target kernel == AWQ and typical seq_len <= 256 and HW in {H100,BW1}, choose lane-packed; else use contiguous. Build a heuristic and simulate routing cost. (Linked JIRA: ENG-4532)
- H2: Implement lightweight runtime transposition for cold-loaded models to allow switching layout without retraining/quantization. Cost to transpose weights offline vs transposition-on-load needs measurement.

Action items / next runs

- [ ] Re-run AWQ+lane-packed on 70B with extended prompt set focusing on numerics (owner: Sofia). Target date: 2027-09-07.
- [ ] Add microbench of transposition cost for 13B/70B on BW1 and H100 (owner: Ethan).
- [ ] Prototype layout flag in runtime and run A/B canary in staging for low-traffic tenant (owner: Rajat).
- [ ] Add additional perf counters: DRAM read/write bytes and L1 hit rates to see if improvements are cache-local or DRAM-bound.

Risks / notes

- Lane-packing increases model on-disk size slightly due to alignment padding; need to check storage impact for Dedicated and Private deployments.
- Potential compatibility issues with some third-party quant tooling that assumes row-major weights. Plan to support both but prefer layout-aware conversion tools.

Appendix: raw numbers (median across 3 runs)

- open-13B / H100 / fused-matmul / AWQ / contiguous: throughput 24.1k tok/s, p95 183 ms, p99 320 ms, quality delta +0.2%
- open-13B / H100 / fused-matmul / AWQ / lane-packed: throughput 28.4k tok/s, p95 165 ms, p99 290 ms, quality delta +0.3%
- open-13B / A100 / fused-matmul / GPTQ / contiguous: throughput 20.2k tok/s, p95 190 ms
- open-70B-lite / BW1 / vectorized-ntt / AWQ / lane-packed: throughput 4.3k tok/s, p95 980 ms, p99 1620 ms (p99 -22% vs contiguous)

Notes on reproducibility

- Harness and runner are checked into the bench folder. Re-run recipe: scripts/bench/quant_layout_sweep --model open-13B --quant awq --layout lane-packed --kernel fused-matmul --hw h100 --repeat 3
- See linked GitHub PR for the compilation flags used.

Questions for discussion at next runtime sync (2027-09-05)

- Are we comfortable shipping lane-packed conversions as an option in Convert-to-Redwood pipeline?
- Tradeoff guardrails: when should the console recommend contiguous vs lane-packed to end-users?
